weighing.summary: The plan lists midnight and 02:00 and recommends 02:00. Neither value has a source I could read. The division commander, Humphreys, wrote in August 1863 that the division was 'bivouacking at 1 a. m. on July 2 about 1 mile from Gettysburg'. Fifteen years later he wrote privately that it 'reached the ground towards midnight of July 1st'. The report of 1863 is the better class of writing and gives the end of the march (settling into bivouac); the letter gives 'reached the ground' and may mean the head of the column, but nothing says so, so the rule that the report of the time beats the memory is applied and 01:00 is the default. The later books that say 1 a.m. (1878, 1900, 1913) name no source, and Bachelder in 1873 says midnight, so they do not add a witness. Nothing gives 02:00. The third brigade is a separate event at 09:00 (Humphreys and Burling).
weighing.who: Humphreys commanded the division and gives its movements under his own orders, with the Black Horse Tavern detour he describes. Burling commanded the third brigade, which was left at Emmitsburg. Bachelder (1873, 1878), the New York commission (1900) and the 1913 Meade volume were not present and name no source.
weighing.when: Humphreys' report is dated 16 Aug 1863 (45 days after, within the best written class); his letter to Fitz Lee is from before early 1878, 14 to 15 years later; Burling wrote on 20 Aug 1863. The books are 10 to 50 years later.
weighing.where: Humphreys rode with the division through the detour and the night march and bivouacked with it. The report says 'bivouacking', the end of the march, a mile from Gettysburg, east of the Emmitsburg road, not on Cemetery Ridge; the letter says 'reached the ground'. Whether they are the same moment is not stated.
weighing.how_knew: Humphreys: his own division, own orders, eyewitness, with a round hour ('1 a. m.'). The letter is a recollection. The later books give no basis.
weighing.clock: Humphreys is Union and uses a plain hour without saying whose watch; no clock correction is applied, and the plan's note of about 20 minutes between the armies' clocks plays no part for a Union witness. The 1 a.m. is a round hour: it may stand for the quarter or half hour around it.
weighing.independence: One line of knowledge carries 01:00: Humphreys' report. Bachelder's letter of 1878, the New York volume and the 1913 book repeat it without a source and are counted with it, so the default carries a single_source flag. Humphreys' letter and Bachelder's 1873 'midnight' are one other line (Bachelder gives no source and may have had the hour from Humphreys). The 09:00 junction of the third brigade is independent: Humphreys and Burling are two reports.

source_panel_text: About 01:00 on Jul 2: General Humphreys' own report of Aug 1863 has his division bivouacking a mile from Gettysburg at 1 a.m. His letter of 1878 says 'towards midnight', a later memory; no source found gives the plan's 02:00. The brigade left at Emmitsburg joined at 9 a.m. Four other values are listed.
